Start simple, practise often, recover well

Best Workout Split for Beginners

Short answer: Most beginners do best on a full-body split two or three days a week, or upper/lower on four days. These plans give you frequent practice on the main lifts without the fatigue of a six-day body-part routine.

What the goal demands from a split

When you are new to lifting, the limiting factor is not volume — it is learning the movements and building the habit of showing up. A good beginner split therefore trains every major movement pattern several times a week at modest volume.

That is why high-volume body-part plans like the bro split or the Arnold split are rarely a good first choice. They give you one session per muscle each week, so you get little practice, and they pile on volume you do not yet need.

What matters most

Practise the main patterns often

Squat, hinge, push and pull each get trained two or three times a week. Repetition is how technique becomes automatic.

Keep volume modest

Two or three hard sets per exercise and five to seven exercises per session is plenty. You are building a base, not chasing a plateau.

Progress in small steps

Add a rep or a small amount of weight when you hit the top of your rep range. Steady increments beat big jumps.

Protect the habit

Choose the number of days you can keep up for months. Three consistent days beat five irregular ones.

Best split by training days

DaysSplitWhy
2 daysFull body A/BEach muscle trained twice a week with long recovery.
3 daysFull body (Mon/Wed/Fri)The classic beginner plan — three weekly exposures to every pattern.
4 daysUpper/lowerA good step up once three days feels easy.

MonFull Body A

ThuRest

Common mistakes

  • Training five or six days a week from day one.
  • Switching programs every few weeks.
  • Adding weight faster than your technique can handle.
  • Skipping legs or pulling exercises because they feel harder.

FAQ

How many days a week should a beginner train?

Two to four. Three full-body days is the most common starting point.

Should beginners do push pull legs?

It can work, but on three days it trains each muscle only once a week. Full body gives more practice for the same days.

How long should I stay on a beginner split?

Until progress stalls despite good effort and recovery — often several months. Do not change just because you are bored in week three.
